info.description:
Better Metadata - Better Science

The submission server takes CEDAR metadata to the repositories that expect it in their own
shape: NCBI BioSample and AIRR, ImmPort, and LINCS.

Two things happen here. Validation converts a CEDAR instance into the target format and returns
that repository's own verdict on it, sending nothing. Submission receives a package of files a
chunk at a time, assembles it, and forwards it once the last chunk lands — so a successful
response means the chunk was stored and any submission it completed was started, not that the
repository has accepted anything.
info.title: CEDAR Submission Server API

post.description: Receive the files of an ImmPort submission, assemble them in CEDAR, and once they are all present submit them to the named workspace. The package arrives a chunk at a time, so a caller sends this repeatedly; the submission starts by itself once the last chunk lands. A 200 therefore means the chunk was stored and any submission it completed was started, not that the repository has accepted anything. While the package is still arriving the response is an empty object rather than a submission result.

200.description: The chunk was stored; ImmPort's result if this completed the submission, an empty object if not

400.description: Not a multipart upload, or no workspace was named

500.description: ImmPort could not be reached, or no ImmPort token is configured

post.summary: Upload a submission package and send it to ImmPort

post.description: The earlier ImmPort path, taking the whole submission as a single multipart request rather than in chunks. Kept for testing from the command line; the chunked route is what the workbench uses.

400.description: Not a multipart upload, or no workspaceId parameter

500.description: ImmPort could not be reached, or no ImmPort token is configured

post.summary: Send a submission to ImmPort in one request

get.description: Ask ImmPort which workspaces the configured account can submit to, and return them. A submission names one of these.

500.description: ImmPort could not be reached, or no ImmPort token is configured

post.description: Receive the files of an AIRR submission, assemble them in CEDAR, and once they are all present send them to NCBI over FTP. The package arrives a chunk at a time, so a caller sends this repeatedly; the submission starts by itself once the last chunk lands. A 200 therefore means the chunk was stored and any submission it completed was started, not that the repository has accepted anything. A package must carry exactly one metadata file. Submissions are sent one at a time, through a queue.

200.description: The chunk was stored; any submission it completed has been started

400.description: Not a multipart upload, or the package does not carry exactly one metadata file

500.description: The chunk could not be stored or the submission could not be prepared

post.summary: Upload an AIRR submission package and send it to NCBI

A 200 therefore means the chunk was stored and any submission it completed was started, not that the repository has accepted anything. A package must carry exactly one metadata file. Submissions are sent one at a time, through a queue.

post.description: Convert a CEDAR instance of the AMIA 2016 demo BioSample template into NCBI's BioSample submission XML and validate that, returning the validator's report. Kept for the template that demo used; new work validates against the generic NCBI route. A controlled term where the template expects a literal is tolerated rather than rejected, since instances in the wild carry them.

500.description: The instance could not be converted to BioSample XML

post.summary: Validate an AMIA 2016 demo BioSample instance

post.description: Convert a CEDAR AIRR instance into the NCBI submission XML and validate it, returning the report. Validation only: nothing is sent to NCBI here.

400.description: The instance could not be read as an AIRR submission

500.description: The submission XML could not be generated

post.summary: Validate an AIRR instance for NCBI

post.description: Forward a CEDAR instance to the LINCS dataset validator and return what it says. The status is the validator's own, so its refusal is reported as it reported it, and CEDAR adds no judgement of its own.

400.description: The LINCS validator rejected the instance

500.description: The LINCS validator could not be reached

post.summary: Validate an instance against the LINCS validator

post.description: Convert a CEDAR instance into the NCBI BioSample submission XML and validate it, returning the report. Validation only: nothing is sent to NCBI here. This is the generic route, which works from the instance's own template rather than a fixed one.
